index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..030c3a6f22e8f04e8b696594506fff472bf51e93 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -371,12 +371,47 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
 
+    Words in capitals, such as acronyms, are kept as they are, unless the
+    whole string is in capitals::
+
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+      >>> titleize("NASA rocket launch")
+      'NASA Rocket Launch'
+      >>> titleize("THE LORD OF THE RINGS")
+      'The Lord Of The Rings'
+
     """
-    return re.sub(
+    title = re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
         humanize(underscore(word)).title()
     )
+    return _restore_acronyms(word, title)
+
+
+def _restore_acronyms(word: str, title: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Put the acronyms of ``word`` back into ``title``, the titleized ``word``.
+
+    An acronym is a word of two or more characters in capitals, like ``NASA``
+    or the ``HTML`` of ``HTMLTidy``. If ``word`` has no lowercase letters,
+    acronyms can't be told from other words, so ``title`` is left as it is.
+    """
+    if not any(char.islower() for char in word):
+        return title
+    words = re.findall(r"[^\W_]+", _underscore_keeping_case(word))
+    if re.search(r"_id$", underscore(word)):
+        words.pop()  # humanize() drops the "_id" suffix
+    parts = re.split(r"([^\W_]+)", title)
+    # A few Unicode case mappings split a word, e.g. "İ".lower() is "i" plus a
+    # combining dot, and then the words of title can't be matched up.
+    if len(parts) != 2 * len(words) + 1:
+        return title
+    for index, original in enumerate(words):
+        if len(original) > 1 and original.isupper():
+            parts[2 * index + 1] = original
+    return ''.join(parts)

     word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
